sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic civil law system; commercial companies governed by the modified Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as subsequently amended, including the 2016 reform introducing the SCSp)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg maintains an extensive double-tax-agreement network, including DTAAs with France, Germany, Belgium, Netherlands, United States, United Kingdom, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Switzerland, UAE and Mauritius
Bilateral investment treaties concluded by the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) and still in force, supplemented by intra-EU investment protections under EU law
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) and the EU Tax Arbitration Convention for cross-border tax disputes
Agreements on the mutual administrative assistance in tax matters, including the OECD/COE Multilateral Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE), as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and applicable CSSF circulars on AML/CFT; transposition of EU Directives (EU) 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673; law on the Freezing of Terrorist Assets and the Grand-Ducal regulations implementing EU and UN sanctions
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Partially_Public_Authorities_And_Legitimate_Interest_Access: registration in the RBE is mandatory for all entities registered in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; access by the general public is restricted to authorities, obliged entities and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest under Luxembourg data-protection and proportionality principles

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO, general partner and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry, passport authority or competent issuing ministry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention where applicable, otherwise Consular Legalization at a Luxembourg consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address and, where applicable, source of funds declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, utility provider, or notary in the jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate partner or corporate UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registry certification followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Organizational chart detailing the full ownership chain through to the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant, certified by the proposed General Partner, with annexes for each corporate layer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certificate followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where required by the receiving Luxembourg notary or bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to the Luxembourg notary and corporate service provider for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and each UBO, executed before a notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft constitutional deed and limited partnership agreement (Statuts / Limited Partnership Agreement) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prepared by Luxembourg counsel; signed by the General Partner and the first limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg notary authentication; supporting signatures and identity documents apostilled as required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, managers and persons exercising control against the Luxembourg RBE manual, CSSF AML typologies, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List and domestic financial security lists. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) screening must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, family members and close associates. For a global IP licensing SCSp, enhanced due diligence is required where royalty flows arise from high-risk third countries or where partners are identified as PEPs, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification with supporting notarized and apostilled documentation. Ongoing transaction monitoring and retention of AML records for at least five years after termination of the business relationship are mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eRCS electronic filing portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; names containing Luxembourgish, French or German words are preferred. Non-Latin script corporate names of foreign partners must be transliterated into standard Latin alphabet for RCS registration. The legal form must appear as 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the recognized abbreviation 'SCSp'. The name must be sufficiently distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS registered name, and must not violate public order or good morals.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (requires CSSF license and Minister of Finance approval)
Société de crédit / Crédit / Clearing / Settlement (requires financial-sector prior authorization)
Fonds commun de placement / Investment Fund / OPC / SICAV / SICAF (requires CSSF recognition)
Trust / Fiduciaire / Trustee (requires professional authorization and is sensitive under AML judgment)
État / Gouvernement / Ministère / Commune / Chambre de commerce (false indication of Luxembourg state or public authority)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / UNESCO or other protected emblems and international organization names
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for approximately two months and is not automatically renewable; upon expiry a fresh reservation application must be submitted in eRCS. If the RCS rejects a name application, the applicant may file a written re-examination request with the LBR Registration Department, attaching evidence of the intended business and precedent usages. If the re-examination is refused, the applicant may submit a corrected new name through eRCS or bring judicial proceedings before the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg to obtain an order directing the registrar to accept the proposed name. The judicial remedy must be lodged within the time limits prescribed by the Luxembourg Code of Civil Procedure and is fact-sensitive.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered-office service with a physical Luxembourg address and a professional domiciliation agent is legally permissible for an SCSp. A purely virtual or desk-only mailbox without any local facility able to receive official service, keep statutory books, and provide records to the Luxembourg authorities will not satisfy RCS registration, AML, or tax substance expectations. For a global IP licensing SCSp, the Luxembourg General Partner or an appointed local managing partner should maintain meaningful decision-making and accounting substance at the registered office, and bank documents should reflect the local address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-medium quantified risk: approximately 5-10% annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection for a passive IP Holding SCSp with clean UBOs, proper bookkeeping and a licensed corporate service provider. Risk rises to 15-25% where UBOs reside in high-risk jurisdictions, royalty flows relate to intangible migration schemes, or the SCSp appears to lack any genuine commercial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT initial due diligence, UBO piercing and PEP/sanctions screening for all natural and corporate partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per screened person and entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation filing through the Luxembourg Business Registers eRCS portal
Apostille and consular legalization of passport copies, address proofs, corporate good-standing certificates and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent ministries, courts or consulates of the issuing jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fees plus courier and translation coordination benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of non-French/German/Luxembourgish documents into the filing language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translators admitted before Luxembourg courts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or market tariff per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notary fees for authentication of the SCSp constitutional deed, partnership agreement and notarized powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg notarial market tariff; corporate notarial work is customarily fee-based

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the SCSp after name clearance and filing of the notarial deed
First-year registered-office and domiciliation services with local corporate agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg corporate service provider / domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual domiciliation fee for an SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence review of IP licensing model, treaty eligibility and Luxembourg economic-substance requirements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement based on complexity and proposed licensing portfolio

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (particularly Articles 1-15, 908-1 to 908-25); Law of 12 July 2013 on Alternative Investment Fund Managers; Law of 13 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) registration application together with notarized or privately signed partnership agreement (statuts) and declaration of conformity
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital requirement for an SCSp; partners may contribute cash, in-kind assets, or services, subject to valuation principles set forth in the partnership agreement; no escrow account is mandated by Luxembourg law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned founding partner, acting for the newly constituted LU_SCSP Special Limited Partnership, hereby RESOLVES THAT: (1) the partnership agreement annexed is approved and adopted in its final form; (2) the registered office of the partnership is established in Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, effective immediately; (3) the subscription and initial contribution arrangements set out in the partnership agreement are accepted and ratified; (4) [Name] is appointed as first manager (gérant) with full and exclusive authority to execute the statutory and regulatory filings; (5) the manager is directed to effect RCS registration, publication, VAT and tax registration, open bank accounts, and carry the business of cross-border patent licensing to operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and reservation with Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS online portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search on the LBR and RCS e-registry against existing company names and registered trademarks; file a name reservation request with up to three alternative names. The name must not infringe public order, misleadingly suggest an activity outside the partnership's object, or confuse the SCSp with another registered entity.
required_dossiers: Duly executed name reservation request form
List of three proposed alternative names
Copy of the founding partner's identification document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR raises a conflict or formal objection, submit amended names or a reasoned legal memorandum proving non-identity with pre-registered marks; request an administrative re-examination within 15 days; thereafter appeal to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Luxembourg bank account and delivery of banker's certificate confirming contribution capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed credit institution in Luxembourg (e.g., Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, BIL, KBL, Société Générale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft partnership agreement, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, and business plan to the selected bank for know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering due diligence; open a Luxembourg sub-account in the name of the SCSp and obtain a banker's confirmation required for the RCS filing where an initial tangible contribution is pledged.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID card of founding partner, general partner, and ultimate beneficial owners
Bank account opening application and KYC/AML forms
Draft partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or letter of domiciliation)
Business description and projected royalty flows for ISIC 6420
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide an organizational chart evidencing the legal structure and audited annual accounts; use a reputable local professional (lawyer, notary, or audit firm) to act as introducer; escalate to the bank's escalation management team in the Grand Duchy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (statuts) and initial corporate acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if the partners elect notarial form) or a registered Luxembourg legal professional for private form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary or under signature of all partners either in person or via power of attorney, specifying the joint venture structure of one or more general partners and at least one limited partner, the legal form (SCSp), the registered office, the share of profits, transfer of partnership interests, and the unconditional duty to make capital contributions as defined. If private deed is used, obtain acknowledgment of good standing.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Identification documents and passport copies of all partners
Certificate of good standing or foreign registry extract for corporate partners
Opinion on legal capacity and signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel identifies invalid or offensive clauses, issue an amendment to the partnership agreement with a supplementary notarial deed or private act signed by the same partners, observing the unanimous consent rule for material modifications prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the RCS registration file electronically through lbr.lu or the notary's secure channel. The application must include the partnership agreement, identification of the general partner and managers, declaration of address/registered office, and the statement that the general partner is not subject to bankruptcy or judicial liquidation. The LBR assigns the registration number and issues an EXTRACT of registration, effective on publication in the Memory or Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement
RCS application form (Form C-Notary or LBR e-form)
Banker's certificate of payment of contributions where applicable
Criminal record extract for each manager or legal representative
Sworn declaration of non-bankruptcy of each manager
Power of attorney if filed via representative
Proof of registered office and domiciliation agreement
Identification of beneficial owner numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR issues a query, correct the deficiencies within 30 days by filing supplemental documents; in case of refusal due to identity of names or non-compliance with statutory form, apply for a formal reconsideration, and thereafter appeal to the competent court, with the right to file a curative application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in RESA and automatic central registry and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for publication; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for corporate and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes the required extract in RESA; simultaneously, the AEDT links the RCS file to the national taxpayer registry and assigns the Luxembourg corporate tax and VAT numbers. Confirm the issuance of a VAT number and request the EORI number if the entity intends to exceed certain trade thresholds, otherwise the VAT exemption for financial holding entities may apply.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of RCS registration extract
RCS registration number
Domiciliation agreement
Identity details of partners for tax purposes
SIEGE declaration confirming the effective tax residence in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays the issuance of the VAT number for an IP holding company, submit a brief statement confirming the future licensing activity and claim VAT registration grounded on the RCS certificate; in case of queries, respond within one month and, if needed, obtain a judicial declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy for guidance; no industrial license required because ISIC 6420 covers asset holding and licensing rather than manufacturing; potential embedded patent licensing activity that is in fact the core activity is considered as a passthrough activity, not an industrial activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt_Class_4 — no full environmental impact assessment required for the mere ownership and licensing of intellectual property; the activity is confined to premium professional offices with no industrial installations, waste processing, or combustion facilities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A — no wastewater discharge, VOC emission point sources, or hazardous industrial waste is generated; office waste is subject to municipal household and commercial waste collections obligations under the General Waste Regulation; foreign patents are administrative assets so no environmental monitoring conditions apply; obligation to implement a takeback scheme for electrical and electronic equipment, should any office equipment be sought, under national WEEE rules

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal commissary (Commune) or the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGFIDS) if the first two floors are occupied; structural load clearance for offices is presumed where the lease complies with the structural safety code; occupational health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) regarding workplace accessibility, electrical installations and the provision of safe working conditions for employees, even if such existence is limited to the general partner's staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes (portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes (portal: https://aedt.public.lu); central e-government portal: myGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu); company registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at https://www.lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident promoter forms an SCSp by private deed (no minimum capital), names a manager (foreign or resident), and files the deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month to obtain the RCS matricule and the statutory national registration number. The SCSp then obtains a Luxembourg tax identification number (numéro d'identification fiscal) from the ACD. For VAT, the SCSp, or a non-established foreign entity making taxable supplies in Luxembourg, must file a VAT registration application (Formulaire de demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT, supported by the RCS extract, deed, partner and manager identification, AML/KYC files (Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier), and a local tax representative where Luxembourg law requires it; registration may also be effected through the myGuichet portal. A foreign entity with no Luxembourg establishment registers directly for a Luxembourg VAT number from the first euro of taxable transactions, subject to reverse-charge and One-Stop-Shop (OSS) mechanisms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (the Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent: it has separate legal personality but is treated as a partnership for income tax purposes, so corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax are not levied at the entity level; profits, losses and tax attributes flow through to the partners, who are taxed according to their own status and country of residence; the SCSp remains a VAT taxable person if it independently and habitually supplies services for consideration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; however, under Article 175 LIR a partnership such as an SCSp may, with the consent of all partners, irrevocably elect for a binding period to be taxed as a capital company (option pour le régime des sociétés de capitaux). VAT-specific elections include the option to form a single VAT unit (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, and the election for group taxation (Fiscal Unity / régime d'intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for corporate income tax and net wealth tax where a 95% parent-subsidiary relationship exists; ATAD 2 hybrid mismatch rules (implemented by the law of 21 December 2020) require the SCSp and its partners to align entity classification elections with EU counterpart jurisdictions to prevent deduction/non-inclusion mismatches and treaty-shopping outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA) implemented under the EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC), with unitary national application and no sub-national sales or use tax in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Established Luxembourg taxable persons: annual turnover exceeding EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT) triggers mandatory VAT registration and filing, with the small-enterprise exemption available below that amount. Non-established foreign suppliers and service providers: no monetary threshold applies, so registration is required from the first euro of taxable supplies in Luxembourg unless the Luxembourg customer accounts for VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism or the supplier uses the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) for cross-border B2C distance sales of goods or electronically supplied services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, no continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance model, no digital stamping obligation, and no state-operated transaction clearance API as of the current filing year. Electronic invoicing is permitted only if authenticity, integrity and readability are ensured; from January 2025, structured electronic invoices (e.g. Peppol BIS or equivalent) must be accepted for Luxembourg public procurement invoices. Luxembourg is aligned with the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) roadmap, which is expected to mandate structured e-invoicing and transaction-based digital reporting from approximately 2030. Currently, compliance is achieved through periodic VAT returns, annual recapitulative EC Sales Lists, Intrastat declarations, and the standard AEDT VAT filing formats.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable - a services-only IP licensing SCSp is not subject to customs formalities unless goods are also dispatched; export-related documentation for any goods is addressed in the export zero-rating section below.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a supply of goods exported to a destination outside the EU qualifies for the 0% export VAT rate (or the corresponding intra-EU dispatch exemption) if the goods are physically dispatched and transported out of the EU by the supplier or on its behalf, and the supplier holds transport and customs evidence (electronic export declaration/EXS, bill of lading/air waybill) demonstrating that the goods left the EU within the legally required period, generally within 90 days. Services: the licensing and sub-licensing of patents, trademarks and other intellectual property by an SCSp to a B2B customer established outside Luxembourg generally has its place of supply at the customer's establishment, so the royalties are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (in practice zero-rated/exempt from Luxembourg VAT); where the customer is established in another EU Member State, the reverse-charge mechanism applies to the customer and the SCSp must issue a VAT invoice stating 'reverse charge' and report the supply in the EC Sales List. For B2C supplies of certain electronically supplied services to non-EU customers, OSS special schemes apply and Luxembourg VAT generally does not apply if the customer resides outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic EXS/Single Administrative Document) evidencing exit from the EU
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch
Commercial invoice referencing the IP licensing contract and the export/zero-rating legal basis
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank remission/FX repatriation evidence) covering the royalty payment
Executed patent/trademark license or sub-license agreement and royalty calculation file
Intercompany transfer pricing documentation supporting arm's length royalty rates
Tax residence certificate of the foreign licensee and, where applicable, a certificate of fiscal domicile of the SCSp's partners
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export documentation is incomplete, untimely or fraudulent, the Luxembourg ACD/AEDT may retroactively assess the supply at the standard 16% VAT, deny the zero-rating or the input VAT deduction/refund, and impose statutory default interest from the due date of the original VAT return. Administrative fines under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law and VAT Law generally amount to up to 10% of the under-declared tax, with higher penalties and criminal sanctions for intentional fraud; the Luxembourg criminal tax fraud framework (in force since 2022) exposes responsible managers and partners to substantial fines and imprisonment for wilful false documentation. The documentation bundle must be retained for the full statutory limitation period, as the tax authorities may re-open assessments within five years (extended in cases of fraud), and retrospective clawbacks may include recharacterization of royalty payments as taxable Luxembourg-source income, reclassification of the SCSp as taxable where the benefit of pass-through treatment is abused under substance-over-form or abuse-of-law (abus de droit) doctrines, and joint and several liability of the manager and partners for the evaded VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); prudential supervision of credit institutions is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while the European Central Bank (ECB) exercises ultimate monetary authority for the euro.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls, prior approvals, surrender duties, or repatriation limits, consistent with TFEU Article 63 free movement of capital. Profit remittances, royalty distributions, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred freely, subject only to bank-level statistical reporting to the BCL (balance of payments / IIP), CRS/DAC6 automatic exchange, and documentary proof of the underlying distribution (notarized partnership resolution for an SCSp). No distinction between current and capital account restrictions exists because both are fully liberalized.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or obligation to surrender export or licensing receipts within any defined period. The SCSp may retain EUR or foreign currency royalty proceeds in designated accounts indefinitely and may convert USD, CHF, or other receipts to EUR at freely negotiated market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore non-EEA EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) used as a primary treasury rail: they lack a Luxembourg or EU PSD2 license or passport, do not participate in BCL balance-of-payments reporting, are outside the Luxembourg banking-secrecy and depositor-protection framework, and frequently restrict or freeze high-value intercompany royalty flows. Medium for EU-licensed EMIs (CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported, e.g., Mangopay, Lemonway) for operational expense disbursements and e-commerce collection, but never for capital escrow, collateral for bank debt, or large-value cross-border clearing. Legal constraints: EMIs may not grant credit, must safeguard client funds separately, and may hold funds only for the duration of the payment order.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person or hybrid physical KYC interview of all authorized signatories and natural-person UBOs (direct or indirect > 25%) is the prevailing bank practice for a Medium-Risk Enhanced IP HoldCo. Remote opening exclusively via video identification is permitted only for Low-Risk structures without non-EEA counterparties; for the SCSp, Tier-1 banks generally require at least one substantive Luxembourg nexus (registered agent with delegated signing authority, local certified director, or an in-person partner meeting at the bank) combined with certified RCS extract, notarized partnership agreement, apostilled corporate documents for non-EU UBOs, and CSSF-compliant KYC files. A remote notarized power of attorney appointing a Luxembourg law firm or regulated fiduciary can substitute for physical UBO appearance only at bank discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is tax-transparent with foreign or corporate general partner (GP), unregulated management structure, and no apparent local substance; flagged as potential shell or tax-evasion vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) certificate, notarized partnership agreement (contrat de société) with GP and partner details, CSSF no-action letter or legal opinion confirming no regulatory license trigger, a substance file evidencing Luxembourg administration (registered office, local bank mandate, minutes of partner meetings held in Luxembourg), and a written commercial rationale for the global patent/trademark licensing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty outflows concentrated toward zero-tax, sanction-sensitive, PEP-related, or high-risk third-country jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed license and sub-license agreements with arm's-length royalty rates supported by OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation (functional analysis, comparability set, interquartile range), tax residency certificates of counterparties, beneficial-ownership registers, sanctions and adverse-media screening reports, and national IP office registration certificates evidencing owned patents/trademarks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal transaction patterns: one-off lump-sum royalty prepayments, round-tripping of injected capital followed by immediate distributions, or cash flows inconsistent with projected royalty curves.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month treasury forecast and business plan, commercial invoices and periodic royalty statements, underlying licensee sales/usage reports, independent valuation report for the contributed or acquired IP, source-of-wealth documentation for the capital contribution, and, if obtained, the approved Luxembourg tax ruling or advance pricing arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared UBOs and payment beneficiaries (payments to third parties not named in the license agreements or to accounts outside the bank).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated UBO declaration and Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, signing-authority matrix (procuration) with clear limits, destination-account confirmation letters signed by each licensee naming the exact IBAN/BIC, and certified bank confirmations for each designated collection and disbursement account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA SCT for EUR) from the contributing shareholder or partner to the SCSp's dedicated IBAN, using ISO 20022 purpose code INVE with narrative 'Contribution en capital — SCSp [entity name]'. Verification protocol at the receiving bank: (1) remitter name must match the partner/shareholder identified in the notarized partnership agreement or capital-contribution resolution; (2) beneficiary name and IBAN must match the RCS extract; (3) amount must align with the approved funding plan and the SCSp's capitalization table; (4) the remitting entity's UBO declaration must be consistent with the RBE/UBO register. The bank records the inflow for BCL monthly balance-of-payments reporting under direct-investment equity (BPM6 standard component F51); no prior exchange-control authorization is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for intercompany royalty and license-fee settlements, referencing ISO 20022 purpose code ROYL or LICF and recorded by the bank under BCL services code S213 (charges for the use of intellectual property). SEPA SCT for eurozone counterparties; SWIFT MT700 (irrevocable documentary letter of credit), MT707 (amendments), and MT798 for commercial settlements where patent licensing is bundled with physical goods, with presentation of commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and transport documents; MT202 COV for nostro clearing of USD/CHF/GBP disbursement legs. All outbound flows require underlying contracts, royalty statements, and invoices retained on file but no foreign-exchange approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, and EUR/GBP FX forwards (typical 3-24 month tenors; ISDA 2002 or local master agreement)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) with EUR or USD cash settlement
FX swaps (simultaneous spot and forward exchange for tenor-matched royalty inflows and disbursements)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intercompany debt and IP acquisition finance
Plain vanilla FX options, including zero-cost collars, to protect minimum royalty conversion rates while retaining upside
Participating forwards and barrier options, permitted only with documented hedge rationale, board-approved treasury policy, and bank credit-line approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts) and deposit with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL), subject to the statutory exemption applicable to SCSp entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved within six months of the balance sheet date and deposited within one month of approval; for a calendar-year SCSp, the effective filing deadline is 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit is sanctioned by fines from EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 (approximately USD 800 to USD 27,000) plus possible daily penalty payments; persistent non-compliance may lead to a court order to file and ultimately administrative strike-off of the entity's RCSL registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax declaration and partner income allocation statement (transparent SCSp informational filing for corporate income tax and municipal business tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May of the year following the tax year for paper filings; e-filing through the ACD eCDF portal extends the deadline to 31 December of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on assessed tax with a EUR 75 minimum, default tax assessment, monthly late-payment interest of 0.8% per month, and, in cases of repeated non-compliance, enforced collection proceedings and lien measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Periodic and annual VAT reconciliation returns covering royalty income derived from cross-border patent and trademark licensing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED), Luxembourg VAT Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns are due by the 12th day of the month following the reporting period; the annual reconciliation return is included in the final taxable period of the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT returns are subject to fines ranging from EUR 150 to EUR 3,000 per declaration, monthly late-payment interest of 0.8%, default VAT assessments, and seizure measures; prolonged failures may trigger administrative enforcement and strike-off procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (UBO/RBE) declaration update and annual confirmation protocol for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change; an annual internal confirmation of the UBO schedule is performed by the general partner and registered agent at the entity anniversary, with a good-practice completion date by 1 April following the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintaining inaccurate RBE information exposes the entity to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 (approximately USD 270,000) and imprisonment of the responsible parties; administrative fines of EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 may also apply, and persistent non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three EU threshold criteria, namely balance sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, and an average of 50 employees; an audited parent entity consolidating the SCSp may also trigger a statutory audit, whereas a 'small' SCSp with below-threshold figures remains exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the law of 19 December 2002 on accounting and annual accounts, implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the European Union is permitted on a voluntary basis for unlisted and non-public-interest partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain a complete internal register of beneficial owners and must file any change in ownership or control with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of the event. Luxembourg law does not impose a fixed annual UBO refiling, but AML/CFT rules require an annual KYC confirmation by the registered agent, which must be documented and followed by an immediate RBE update if any discrepancy is identified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent; a fully taxable Luxembourg corporate partner is subject to 17% corporate income tax plus 7% employment-fund surcharge, and in Luxembourg City the aggregate corporate tax burden including 6.75% municipal business tax is 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level corporate income tax applies to the transparent SCSp. For a taxable corporate partner, qualifying licensing income can benefit from the 80% Luxembourg IP regime exemption, reducing the effective aggregate tax rate on qualifying net IP royalties to approximately 4.99% where substance, nexus and documentation conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1622 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the eCDF electronic portal of the Administration des contributions directes; municipal business tax and net wealth tax declarations are coordinated in the same annual filing package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year taxpayers must file by 31 March of the following year, with an extension to 31 December obtainable on request before the original deadline; non-calendar-year taxpayers must file within the same statutory framework based on the accounting period and any ACD tax summons.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS file number, tax file number, registered office and legal form; must match the Luxembourg trade register and the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A transparent SCSp normally has no standalone corporate income tax file; non-resident partners are taxable on their allocated profit share in their state of residence unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income per the audited annual accounts after commercial law adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the transparent SCSp itself; no entity-level corporate profit is computed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disallowed expenses, tax-exempt income, IP-regime deduction, participation exemption, notional interest deduction and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner applies Luxembourg adjustments only where the SCSp gives rise to a Luxembourg taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit absorbed by available carry-forward losses; Luxembourg restricts annual set-off to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are attributed to partners and utilised under their domestic tax rules; the SCSp does not file a consolidated loss position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits, and other refundable or creditable tax amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are claimed in the partner's residence country; the SCSp reports only allocable income and does not claim tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a compulsory assessment, late-payment interest at 0.8% per month, a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed corporate income tax, and administrative fines; deliberate misdeclaration constitutes tax fraud and is punishable by fines up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment in aggravated cases.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax for taxable company distributions; SCSp profit distributions to partners are not treated as dividends and are therefore not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax. The 15% rate may be reduced to 0% under the Luxembourg participation exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or an applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The SCSp has no treaty entitlement because it lacks legal personality and is not a Luxembourg tax resident. Non-resident partners must claim treaty relief on their allocated income by providing a tax residence certificate from their state of residence, completing the relevant Luxembourg relief or refund claim form, and demonstrating beneficial ownership and substance; the ACD issues Luxembourg residency certificates only for filers that are actually taxable in Luxembourg.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalty or interest payments; the domestic rate is 0%. Treaty rates are therefore generally not required to invoke Luxembourg relief, but the paying entity must maintain evidence of beneficial ownership and the commercial reality of the transaction to prevent anti-abuse recharacterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File obligation is generally triggered when the Luxembourg entity belongs to a group with annual consolidated turnover above EUR 50,000,000 and has intra-group transactions; Master File and Country-by-Country Report obligations apply above EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue. The ACD may also request transfer pricing documentation under Article 56 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law regardless of formal thresholds where controlled transactions are material.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulation in the format used by offshore financial centres, but substance is central to Luxembourg and EU anti-abuse rules, including ATAD Article 6, the Luxembourg General Anti-Abuse Rule, OECD functional analysis, treaty beneficial-ownership requirements, and the IP regime nexus requirements. An SCSp licensing patents or trademarks must demonstrate active management, local decision-making, qualified staff, premises, risk control and real economic activity; a paper-only IP conduit is exposed to recharacterisation and denial of treaty and domestic tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of royalty income, fabrication of deductible licensing costs, use of sham invoices, or deliberate concealment of a Luxembourg permanent establishment through a transparent SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment with interest, penalties of 20% to 100% of the evaded tax, criminal fines of up to EUR 10,000, imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud, withdrawal of tax incentives, and publication in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and managing directors who knowingly participate are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax; criminal convictions may add disqualification, personal fines, travel bans and asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp with no staff, no local management, no operational office and no substantive control over sub-licensed patents and trademarks, while routing global royalty income through Luxembourg solely to exploit treaty and IP tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may disregard the SCSp, reallocate royalty income to the ultimate licensor under Article 56 LIR and ATAD GAAR, deny treaty benefits, apply ordinary corporate tax plus penalty interest, and refuse the IP regime exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are exposed to civil liability for breach of fiduciary duty, damages for reckless facilitation of the abusive structure, and, in egregious cases, personal liability for the reassessed tax deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misleading use of the SCSp to conceal ultimate beneficial owners, failure to maintain UBO registers, and executing royalty wires to shell counterparties without proper customer due diligence or transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties of up to EUR 1,000,000 for entities and up to 10% of annual turnover in serious cases; responsible natural persons face fines and imprisonment; the CSSF or Luxembourg public prosecutor may order transaction freezing and suspension of business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners and senior officers are personally liable for AML violations, including criminal penalties, travel restrictions, temporary bans from exercising managerial functions, and seizure of personal assets where money laundering is proven.
